text.p: The following are the main stories from Thursday morning's Austrian newspapers:
DER STANDARD

- 58 percent of Austrians say designated chancellor Viktor Klima is able to solve Austria's problems better compared to only 15 percent saying chancellor Franz Vranitzky could do it better, a poll by market-institute shows.

- Klima's top candidate for finance minister, Burgenland's state leader Karl Stix, is proving to be a hard choice as Burgenland's People's Party, junior coalition partner in the state's government, wants to have a say on who will become the next state leader. The conservatives are threatening siding with the far-right Freedom Party in Burgenland.
- The mayor of Wiener Neustadt, Peter Wittmann, will become the new state secretary following Karl Schloegl's move to the Interior Ministry.
- Union secretary Herbert Tumpel will become the new Workers' Union president as its former President Eleonore Hostasch will take over the Social Affairs Ministry.
- The highest price rises in Austria were recorded in state-influenced sectors.
- Austrian industry plans to invest 10 percent more this year than last due to improved sentiment and turnover.
- Savings banks' union is against paying a provision for municipal liabilities.
- Papermaker KNP Leykam will cut 1,000 jobs by 1999, half of which will be in Austria. The rationalisation is expected to save about 630 million schillings per year.
DIE PRESSE
- Austria's trade deficit is growing as imports from other EU-members rose 5.2 percent in the first half of 1996. The overall trade deficit was 54.9 billion schillings in the same period.
- While AVZ, the major shareholder in GiroCredit, wants to sell its GiroCredit shares at 400 schillings per share, Die Erste savings bank does not want to pay that price.

- Should the ruling government coalition split up within the next three years, Bank Austria could already completely merge with Creditanstalt by 2000, even though it has said it would let Creditanstalt remain independent for at least five years.
- Bank Austria will become the largest savings bank worldwide, pushing Italy's Cariplo into second, if the EU commission gives the go ahead for its takeover of Creditanstalt.
- Economic research institute Wifo expects labour tax to be reduced while fees are likely to rise.
- The fall in income of Austria's farmers by 6.9 percent in 1996 is the greatest fall in comparison to other countries in the EU.
KURIER
- New state secretary Peter Wittmann will take over the art portfolio from Caspar Einem's new Transport, Art and Science Ministry.
- Austria's oil group OMV and RAG, which is majority-owned by regional utility EVN, see no chance of a joint gas-pipeline to the German border.
WIRTSCHAFTSBLATT
- Vienna should become the centre for Eastern European shares, strategists of OeTOB, Austrian futures and options exchange say.
- Fire-engine maker Rosenbauer's profits remained stable in 1996 as 1995's profits were 1.94 billion schillings.
